findings.suggested_repair: Render inline mathematics in proof-technique metadata, or replace the TeX fragments with prose.

diagram_candidates.kind: candidate; optional explanatory TikZ characteristic-projection diagram
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The example explicitly contrasts the injective classical projection before t=1/2 with its loss of injectivity and the two Hopf–Lax minimisers after that time. A small three-time characteristic sketch would make the fold and resulting corner easier to inspect. It is a pedagogical suggestion, not a mathematical defect.
diagram_candidates.specific_content_to_draw_or_check: Use horizontal y and vertical x_t=X_t(y). Show a monotone curve for 0≤t<1/2, the horizontal tangent X_{1/2}'(0)=0 at the critical time, and for t>1/2 the fold with X_t(-s_t)=X_t(0)=X_t(s_t)=0, s_t=√log(2t). In a companion x,t panel mark x=0 with the two minimizing branches y=±s_t and the unequal one-sided slopes ∓s_t/t; keep the characteristic projection distinct from the minimizer relation.
diagram_candidates.certainty: high-likelihood optional explanatory diagram; no required correction

diagram_candidates.kind: candidate; optional explanatory TikZ spacetime cone diagram
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The definition organizes the domain of dependence around a backward cone, its base ball, and a lateral boundary; a spacetime picture is a high-likelihood aid to locating these sets. This is optional and not a defect.
diagram_candidates.specific_content_to_draw_or_check: In one spatial dimension draw axes x and t, vertex (x_0,t_0), backward characteristic edges x=x_0±c(t_0−t) down to the base interval [x_0−ct_0,x_0+ct_0] at t=0, and shade K^-(x_0,t_0) with the base ball/slice and lateral boundary labelled. If showing the forward cone too, use x=x_0±c(t−t_0) for t≥t_0 and label it separately. Preserve whether cone/base surfaces are closed.
